Think a pay rise could leave you worse off? It can’t.
Only the extra pay above the new rate gets taxed at the higher rate.
Everything below stays the same.
So yes, take the raise. You’re still ahead.
#wages
#costofliving
#tax 
#bracketcreep

Ever heard that you could be worse off after a pay rise? In Australia’s tax system, that’s impossible.

You’ll always take home more when your wages go up, even if you enter a new tax bracket 💸

The best way to get the pay rise you deserve is to build power at work by joining your union.

So, if you’re not a member yet, it’s time to join! Link in bio 🔗

A huge thank you to Sally McManus and Michele O’Neil following the announcement that they will step down as Secretary and President of the Australian Council of Trade Unions.

Sally and Michele have been remarkable leaders of the trade union movement. Their contributions across almost a decade of leadership will be felt by Australian workers and their families for generations to come.

Under Sally and Michele’s leadership, the union movement successfully fought off attempts by the Turnbull and Morrison governments to reduce and undermine the rights of Australian workers.

Since then, with Sally and Michele at the helm workers have benefitted from dozens of new workplace rights which have raised wages, reduced the gender pay gap, delivered more secure jobs, and made workplaces safer.

For the South Australian union movement, Sally and Michele have been more than national leaders - they have been steadfast allies and comrades to South Australian workers. 

We thank Sally and Michele for their tireless work on behalf of working people and wish them both the very best for the future.

When someone gets hurt doing their job, they deserve support to recover, stay connected to work, and avoid financial hardship.

Too many workers dealing with South Australia’s compensation system face delays, poor communication, and unfair barriers which stop them receiving the support they need.

An upcoming independent review of the Return To Work system is a major opportunity to re-build our compensation system.

People with direct experience of the system know where it’s failing and what needs to change.

That’s why we need to hear your story – to fight for a system that treats injured workers as people, not just claim numbers.

Share your experiences through our online survey and help us create a compensation system that delivers dignity, fairness, and respect.

Complete the online survey today - link in bio 🔗

Be part of organising Reclaim the Night 2026.

Reclaim the Night is a global movement calling for an end to gendered violence, harassment and victim-blaming, while working towards safer and more just communities.

Whether you're a worker, student, activist or simply passionate about creating safer communities, there are many ways to get involved.

📅 First planning workshop:
Wednesday 12 August
5:30 pm – 7:30 pm

The Collective will then meet on Wednesday evenings from August to October to organise Reclaim the Night 2026.

Register via the link in our bio to stay updated about upcoming meetings and opportunities to get involved.

All women and gender-diverse people are welcome. Our Collective is proudly trans-inclusive and sex worker–inclusive.

Congratulations to @abcadelaide's Sophie Holder for winning the Max Fatchen Award for Best Young Journalist at the 2026 SA Media Awards!

SA Unions is proud to sponsor this award because young journalists like Sophie are the future of an ethical, independent, and strong media here in South Australia.

The SA Media Awards are made possible by @withmeaa, the union for media professionals which works tirelessly to support journalists and safeguard the future of the industry.

Congratulations again to Sophie on her well-deserved win!

We were proud to join union workers celebrating Fifty Years of Deadly at the NAIDOC March today ✊

It’s a privilege to stand together with Elders who have built this movement, young leaders who are taking up the fight for justice, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander workers who are leading change across every field.

There’s still time to apply to be part of Organising Works in 2027 📢

Organising Works is a national training and leadership development program run by the Australian Council of Trade Unions. 

Across a 12-month paid traineeship, you’ll learn how to build worker power and win alongside members through a combination of education and real-world organising experience. 

The course is designed for anyone committed to social change and collective action and is a great opportunity for delegates, HSRs, and union activists ✊

Applications close this Sunday 12 July. 

Find out more - link in bio🔗

Join union members at the NAIDOC March this Friday 10 July as we celebrate fifty years of NAIDOC Week.

For five decades, NAIDOC Week has celebrated First Nations culture, called for truth, and honoured resistance. This year’s theme - Fifty Years of Deadly - is a tribute to the people who built this movement and a commitment to continue the work.

We’re kicking off at 10:30am at Tarntanyangga (Victoria Square) and marching up King William St to Parliament House.

Stick around at Tarntanyangga after the march to enjoy music, food, market stalls, and activities for the kids at the NAIDOC Family Festival until 3:30pm.

Come along to stand in solidarity with Elders who have led the way and young people who are carrying on the fight for justice with new tools and the same fire.

When working South Aussies need leaders to have their back, One Nation are talking about cutting their jobs, not lifting their pay
#wages #costofliving #housingcrisis #minimumwage  #penaltyrates

The cost of living keeps rising, and wages at the bottom simply aren’t keeping up.

We welcome the national increase to minimum wage and awards, and we’re also backing the call for a 6% boost to minimum wages for SA workers in the state system. 

It’s time to close the gap between pay packets and the real cost of living.

Are you feeling the squeeze right now?

We asked One Nation if they support a pay rise for the lowest-paid workers in South Australia’s public schools and hospitals 🤔

We didn’t think that was a hard question.

They said they were focused on cutting government services instead. 

Two weeks after Pauline Hanson called Australian workers lazy and talked about scrapping important protections, One Nation politicians in SA can't even stick up for the workers who keep our essential services running. 

Some of the lowest-paid workers in SA do the most important jobs for our community.

That’s why union members are calling for a 6% increase to SA’s minimum wage 📢
